title: Analysis code and data: applying a Bayesian priority-action score to India's drug-resistant tuberculosis surveillance, 2017-2024
description:
Complete analysis code, input data and outputs for a study applying a Bayesian priority-action score to India's drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) surveillance over 2017-2024.

Surveillance data. Five national DR-TB axes reconstructed from the World Health Organization Global TB Programme country data for India (notifications, treatment outcomes, drug-resistance surveillance and burden-estimate datasets, retrieved 8 September 2026). data/ntep_trajectories.csv carries, for every datapoint, its numerator, its denominator, the WHO field names it was derived from and its source dataset, so each value is traceable to a published field rather than to a summary table.

Literature data. data/tb_interventions_unified.csv is a 3,589-record open-access harvest (twelve Boolean queries, one per pre-specified intervention node, against PubMed E-utilities and Europe PMC, 20 May 2026).

Code. code/build_tb_bopas_ijtb.py fits the trajectories with bootstrap and t-based intervals, segments them at documented reporting breaks, codes the corpus with a corrected direction-of-effect classifier, computes the score, and emits six sensitivity scenarios. It is pure-Python 3.11 with no third-party numerical dependency; the incomplete beta function is evaluated by continued fraction and inverted by bisection, and verification/test_beta_bound.py checks that implementation and every published credible bound against SciPy.

Verification. The scripts under verification/ re-check word counts, keyword rules, citation sequence, blinding and every reported number against the pipeline outputs. Those under validation/ build and analyse a stratified 150-record worksheet for validating the automated classifier against independent human coding.

Version 1.1.0. Adds code/trend_component.py (the surveillance-trend term of the score under alternative analytic choices, written to outputs/trend_component.json) and the completed validation of the automated direction-of-effect classifier: validation/validation_codes_final.csv holds, for 150 record-intervention pairs, the classifier code, two coders' independent codes and the final consensus code (identifiers and codes only), and validation/summarise_validation_final.py writes outputs/validation_final.json. The coders agreed on 141 of 150 pairs (Cohen's kappa 0.90); 95 of 150 pairs did not evaluate the intervention they had been assigned to, and on the 55 genuine evaluations the classifier's direction matched the consensus in 29. The literature-evidence term of the score is therefore not supported by this classifier.

Version 1.1.1. Adds WHO's zoonotic tuberculosis dataset (data/who_zoonotic_tb_2026-11-26.csv, collected for 2018 and 2023) and code/zoonotic_reporting.py, which writes outputs/zoonotic_reporting.json: India reported no speciation results for pulmonary or extrapulmonary TB in 2018 and answered that no one was diagnosed with zoonotic TB in 2023, when 34 of 204 responding countries reported zoonotic diagnoses.

Version 1.2.1. Adds WHO's drug-resistance surveillance dataset (data/who_dr_surveillance_2026-11-26.csv) and a test of whether a shift between new and previously treated patients explains the 2021 rise in rifampicin resistance: the rise appears in both groups and among all tested patients (new_vs_previously_treated and segmented_2021 in outputs/revision_analyses.json).

Version 1.2.0. Adds analyses requested in peer review (code/revision_analyses.py, output outputs/revision_analyses.json): segmented models with t intervals for every series at its reporting break, rifampicin-testing and cohort coverage, outcome composition by cohort, validation sensitivity analyses against the pre-check consensus and each coder with Wilson intervals, and the full distribution of WHO zoonotic answers. Archives the WHO country files used (data/who_2026-08-25/), the pre-check consensus and AI-assisted recoding in validation/validation_codes_final.csv, and the recoding instructions (validation/ai_blind_recode_prompt.md).

Principal finding. No axis of India's DR-TB surveillance is significantly worsening over the period; treatment success improved by +4.23 (MDR/RR-TB) and +6.38 (XDR-TB) percentage points per year. The score returns no urgent priority. Fitting across an uncorrected 2021 reporting discontinuity is sufficient on its own to manufacture a confident top-ranked priority on an axis that is in fact improving.
